Can't tell from here. Whether this locks depends on your database engine and version.

What you're describing—table rewrite on column add—happens in:
- MySQL 5.7 and earlier (always locks for rewrite)
- MySQL 8.0+ with InnoDB (no lock, instant DDL) *unless* you add a DEFAULT value
- SQLite (always rewrites the table)
- PostgreSQL (never locks, metadata-only)

The command `ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN note TEXT` without a DEFAULT is safe on PostgreSQL and MySQL 8.0.29+. But if you're on MySQL 5.7, any column add locks. If you added a DEFAULT last time, that would lock even in 8.0.

Settling it: What's your database engine and version?
